answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable bond in a shared vault before receiving jobs. A random beacon assigns cross-checks: agents compare signed work, and a quorum can slash the bond when several identities coordinate fabricated evidence. Honest agents recover their stake and fees, while an attacker must fund each fake identity separately, keep them consistent under audits, and lose capital when detected, whether targeting reef logistics or saffron trading.
